永.meaning: A single <part>dot</part> on a museum map says 'You are here', so a tourist stands on that spot by a fountain of <part>water</part> and waits for the tour guide. The guide never comes. Ivy climbs his legs, the fountain keeps splashing, and the dot still says he's here. He has been waiting an <kanji>eternity</kanji>.
永.on: Squirrels bury an <sound>a</sound>corn by his shoes, and an oak grows up past his shoulders.
永.kun: Pigeons nibble the <sound>na</sound>an in his pocket, and his beard trails down into a bed of <sound>ga</sound>rlic.

幻.meaning: At a laundromat at 3 a.m., a sleepy man watches his socks spin. One sock floats out of the drum, does a slow <part>twist</part> in the air, bows to him and waltzes out the door. He rubs his eyes: the door is locked and the sock is back in the pile. It was a <kanji>phantasm</kanji>.
幻.on: His sleepy friend <sound>Gen</sound> saw the waltz too, so they both agree it never happened.
幻.kun: He phones his <sound>ma</sound>ma, who once saw a <sound>bo</sound>ttle ride a <sound>ro</sound>cket over her <sound>shee</sound>p.

拡.meaning: A baker's shop is too cramped for her queue, so she hooks an <part>anchor</part> into the back wall and lets a tugboat pull. With a groan the walls stretch, and the shop grows <part>wide</part> enough for a dance floor. Every busy morning she has the tug <kanji>broaden</kanji> it a little more.
拡.on: The tug's crew snack on a picked-clean chicken <sound>carc</sound>ass while they wait for her signal.
拡.kun: The queue spreads out the door: a lady in high <sound>hee</sound>ls, a boy with a toy <sound>ro</sound>cket, then half the town.

富.meaning: A burglar sneaks under the <part>roof</part> of a sweet old lady's house hunting for jewels, but finds only a <part>cookie jar</part>. Under the biscuits are the deeds to three castles and a racehorse. Granny's <kanji>wealth</kanji> was sitting by the teapot all along.
富.on: The rest of her money is stuffed inside her <sound>fu</sound>ton, which is why it crackles.
富.kun: A little <sound>to</sound>tem pole of gold coins stands on the jar's lid.

貧.meaning: A broke hermit crab can't afford a whole house, so he rents one <part>part</part> of an old <part>shellfish</part> shell and shares it with four lodgers. His tail sticks out into the cold wind all night. On the beach, that's real <kanji>poverty</kanji>.
貧.on: The shell's one rusty <sound>hin</sound>ge squeaks every time a lodger rolls over.
貧.kun: His <sound>ma</sound>ma sends him a single yu<sound>zu</sound> for his birthday, and he shares that too.

困.meaning: A magician locks a parrot in a <part>cage</part>, waves his wand, and the parrot turns into a little <part>tree</part>. The crowd claps. He waves again: nothing. The tree drops a leaf on his shoe. He doesn't know the spell to turn it back. What a <kanji>quandary</kanji>.
困.on: A <sound>con</sound>dor lands on the cage and asks if the tree is for rent.
困.kun: He phones a <sound>ko</sound>ala vet, then his <sound>ma</sound>ma. Neither can turn a tree back into a bird.

華.meaning: For the town fair, a farmer wraps a tall <part>pole</part> in <part>grass</part> and flowers, layer on layer, and balances <part>one</part> golden bar across the very top. A goat nibbles the bottom layer as it parades past, and the whole tower bows to the crowd. Even nibbled, it's pure <kanji>splendor</kanji>.
華.on: The tower rides through town on a cart shaped like a huge orange <sound>ca</sound>rp.
華.kun: A band plays a <sound>ha</sound>rp, and the goat moves on to a basket of <sound>na</sound>an.

豪.meaning: A giant <part>pig</part> sits on a picnic <part>blanket</part>, a pot <part>lid</part> on its head like a crown, and opens its <part>mouth</part> to sneeze. The blast flattens the sandwiches, the trees and an ants' nest down the hill. Nobody argues with a sneeze that <kanji>overpowering</kanji>.
豪.on: Only a <sound>goa</sound>t stays standing, calmly chewing the blanket's corner.
豪.kun: The pig is crowned king of the picnic: the crowd throws an <sound>e</sound>gg sandwich and shouts '<sound>Rah</sound>!'

悩.meaning: The <part>villain</part> whose plan lit up the sky lies awake. Each time he shuts his eyes, <part>fireworks</part> go off over his bed and his <part>heartbeat</part> races. He counts sheep, but the sheep line up as a jury. He's in big <kanji>trouble</kanji>.
悩.on: Outside the window, the garden <sound>gno</sound>me who called the police waves at him all night.
悩.kun: He creeps down for some <sound>na</sound>an, and a voice in the dark says '<sound>Yah</sound>, we're still watching.'

伏.meaning: At a royal dog show, a scruffy <part>dog</part> hangs his collar on a <part>coat hook</part> by the stage, then flops flat on the floor before the queen, belly down, nose on her slippers. The judges are charmed. He wins the prize for lying the most <kanji>prostrated</kanji>.
伏.on: His prize ribbon hangs from the same <sound>hook</sound> as his collar.
伏.kun: Then he flops down again, this time on a rolled-up <sound>fu</sound>ton by the door.

削.meaning: A cheese seller takes a <part>dagger</part> to a wheel of cheddar, shaving off curl after curl until the block bears a <part>resemblance</part> to her cat. Customers buy the curls by the bag. Every morning she grabs the blade to <kanji>plane</kanji> a fresh one.
削.on: She sells the curls in pots next to a fat <sound>suc</sound>culent by the till.
削.kun: Then she boils the <sound>ke</sound>ttle and grates a yu<sound>zu</sound> over the last curl.

甲.meaning: A scarecrow is tired of crows pecking him, so he straps a shiny metal <part>sun</part> to his chest, held up by the <part>pole</part> through his middle. Now every beak goes clang. The farmer proudly calls it his scarecrow's <kanji>armor</kanji>.
甲.on: The crows try one last trick: dropping an ice cream <sound>co</sound>ne on it from above.
甲.kun: Then they throw a <sound>ki</sound>wi, a rock that's <sound>no</sound>t small and a rotten <sound>e</sound>gg.

療.meaning: A penguin with a cold waddles into a <part>leaky shed</part> on the ice, where a walrus doctor keeps a <part>bonfire</part> going. The drips sizzle, the penguin sweats out his sniffles, and he leaves with a warm beak. The walrus can <kanji>heal</kanji> anything except melting.
療.on: Next door the walrus runs a little <sound>ryo</sound>kan where cured penguins stay the night.

針.meaning: A hedgehog visits a jeweller and orders <part>ten</part> spines of solid <part>gold</part>. The jeweller files and files, and each spine ends up thin as a hair with a hole at the end. Now she sews her own scarves with every <kanji>needle</kanji> on her back.
針.on: She drops one and it lands point-up, right into the jeweller's <sound>shin</sound>.
針.kun: She uses another to restring a <sound>ha</sound>rp, then knits a hat for a <sound>ree</sound>f fish.

池.meaning: In the desert, a <part>scorpion</part> collects <part>water drops</part> from the morning dew, one at a time, and pours them into a dent in the sand. After a year it's big enough for a frog to swim in, and the scorpion charges ducks to land. It's the only <kanji>pond</kanji> for miles.
池.on: A thirsty <sound>chee</sound>tah tries to sneak a drink without paying.
池.kun: An <sound>ee</sound>l moves in, and the scorpion fills a <sound>ke</sound>ttle from the pond for its tea.

捨.meaning: A sailor retires to a seaside <part>cottage</part> and uses his ship's <part>anchor</part> as a doorstop. His wife trips on it every day. One night she drags it to the cliff and heaves it into the sea with a mighty splash. Some things you just <kanji>discard</kanji>.
捨.on: Next she flings out his old <sound>shu</sound>ttlecock collection, feathers drifting after the anchor.
捨.kun: Then she tosses a tray of week-old <sound>su</sound>shi in after it.

還.meaning: A <part>scuba diver</part> finds a little fish that flopped out of the sea and got lost in a car park. She carries it down the boat <part>ramp</part>, lowers it into the waves and waves goodbye. Every lost sea creature she finds, she makes sure to <kanji>send back</kanji>.
還.on: The fish returns next day with a pink <sound>car</sound>nation in its mouth.
還.kun: She swims home <sound>ca</sound>lm, an <sound>e</sound>gg-shaped pebble in her pocket as its thank-you.

訓.meaning: A swimming teacher gives her lessons from a canoe, shouting a <part>speech</part> to a row of ducklings while the <part>river</part> sweeps them all downstream. By the waterfall, every duckling can paddle backwards. Ducklings get the best <kanji>instruction</kanji>.
訓.on: One duckling naps through the whole lesson wrapped in a silk co<sound>coon</sound>.
訓.kun: Next term she teaches an <sound>o</sound>tter and a very soggy <sound>shee</sound>p.

徴.meaning: Riding a <part>chairlift</part> up a <part>mountain</part>, a weather-mad <part>king</part> watches his folding <part>fan</part>: if it flutters left, snow is coming; if right, soup for lunch. Today it spins in circles. His cooks panic over the mixed <kanji>indications</kanji>.
徴.on: His royal <sound>cho</sound>ker always tightens when a storm is near, and today it's snug.
徴.kun: Then a <sound>shee</sound>p, a <sound>roo</sound>k and a second <sound>shee</sound>p ride up the lift behind him.

仏.meaning: In a quiet mountain garden sits a calm stone figure, one <part>elbow</part> resting on its knee. Hikers hang their wet jackets on a <part>coat hook</part> beside it and sit down too, smiling for no reason, while a sparrow nests in the crook of its arm. Everyone leaves calmer after visiting the <kanji>Buddha</kanji>.
仏.on: A <sound>bu</sound>ll lies down at its feet and stays calm, even when a <sound>tsu</sound>nami roars far below the hill.
仏.kun: A gardener sets a <sound>ho</sound>t cup of tea on <sound>to</sound>p of the wall and refills the <sound>ke</sound>ttle.

索.meaning: A princess locked in a tower unpicks her woolly <part>blanket</part> into <part>thread</part>, then braids <part>ten</part> strands together, over and over, until it's thick enough to hold a horse. She ties it to the bedpost and climbs out the window. Never underestimate a good <kanji>cord</kanji>.
索.on: At the bottom she lands in a pot of prickly <sound>suc</sound>culents.

憎.meaning: A cat's <part>heartbeat</part> spikes whenever the vacuum cleaner comes out. <part>Formerly</part> it chased her round the kitchen and swallowed her favourite toy mouse, and she remembers every second. She hisses at it from the top of the fridge. Pure <kanji>hate</kanji>.
憎.on: She even checks her <sound>zo</sound>diac each morning to see if it's a vacuum day.
憎.kun: She swats the <sound>knee</sound> of the <sound>coo</sound>k who plugs it in.

夢.meaning: Every <part>evening</part> a little girl lies on the <part>grass</part> under a <part>blanket</part> and swings a butterfly <part>net</part> at the stars. Tonight she catches one, and it purrs like a kitten in her hands. Then her alarm rings. It was only a <kanji>dream</kanji>.
夢.on: A <sound>moo</sound>se is licking her face to wake her up.
夢.kun: For breakfast her dad slices a <sound>yu</sound>zu and a <sound>me</sound>lon into star shapes.

浸.meaning: A tea-mad grandpa dunks everything in his tea: his garden <part>rake</part>, his <part>blanket</part>, a salty <part>pretzel</part>, until <part>water drops</part> drip from the ceiling. Grandma finds him sitting in a bath of tea with a teabag on his head. He's fully <kanji>immersed</kanji>.
浸.on: The tea in the bath comes right up to his <sound>shin</sound>.
浸.kun: He dips one <sound>hee</sound>l in, then a crunchy <sound>ta</sound>co.

鬼.meaning: Nobody wants to play the haunting spirit in the school play, so the janitor volunteers. He wears a cardboard <part>skull</part>, wobbles on stilt <part>legs</part>, and sticks out one <part>elbow</part> with a sheet hanging off it. The kids scream, the parents cheer. Best <kanji>ghost</kanji> ever.
鬼.on: Afterwards he can't find the <sound>key</sound> to the cupboard where his own clothes are.
鬼.kun: '<sound>Oh</sound>, my k<sound>nee</sound>!' he groans, climbing down off the stilts.

魔.meaning: A <part>ghost</part> lives in a shed full of drying <part>hemp</part> ropes and teaches itself spells: knots that untie themselves, ropes that slither like snakes. One night it grabs a broom and a pointy hat and zooms out of the chimney. Now it's a <kanji>witch</kanji>.
魔.on: It brews its potions in a chipped <sound>mu</sound>g instead of a cauldron.

樹.meaning: A golfer slices her ball into the forest and, in a temper, whacks a <part>tree</part> with her <part>golf club</part>. It booms like a <part>drum</part>! She whacks another, then ten more, and a music shop owner on the path offers to buy the lot. That forest is now top-grade <kanji>timber</kanji>.
樹.on: A <sound>ju</sound>ry of squirrels decides which trunks sound best.
樹.kun: She finds her ball at last, tucked under a sleeping <sound>ki</sound>wi bird.

織.meaning: A spider in a castle tower uses the <part>war gong</part> as her loom: she strings <part>thread</part> across its face, and every time the soldiers strike it, the shaking jiggles her lines into a tidy pattern. By sunset the gong wears a shawl. She lets war help her <kanji>weave</kanji>.
織.on: When it's struck mid-row, she gets a tingling <sound>shock</sound> up all eight legs.
織.kun: An <sound>o</sound>tter swims up the moat and orders a matching scarf.

塗.meaning: A pig opens an art studio. He mixes <part>soil</part> and <part>water drops</part> into brown goo, then slaps on <part>too much</part> of it, covering the canvas, the easel and the art critic. The critic calls it brave. Mud is the pig's favourite <kanji>paint</kanji>.
塗.on: Next he slathers it all over the <sound>to</sound>tem pole outside the gallery.
塗.kun: Then he crawls into a cosy <sound>noo</sound>k and coats its walls too.

励.meaning: A snail decides to climb a <part>cliff</part>. At the bottom, <part>ten thousand</part> ants wave flags and flex every <part>muscle</part> in their tiny arms, chanting 'Go! Go!' It takes him a week, but he reaches the top. That's what it means to <kanji>encourage</kanji>.
励.on: At the top, a <sound>ray</sound> leaps up out of the sea below to give him a high five.
励.kun: A <sound>ha</sound>rp plays, and a <sound>ge</sound>cko scurries up beside him to try next.
